body.statement:
Fix \(n\).  For \(g\in E_k\), let \(b_{gk,q}\) denote the expression inside square brackets in the definition of \(c_{kq}\), let
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),
 \qquad
 \tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and define the exact block remainder \(r_{gk}\) by
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk}.
\]
Then the eligible-unit aggregation obeys the exact eventwise identity
\[
 D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
For \(C>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)=\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
 \{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), the deterministic implication
\[
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)
\]
holds.  In the i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel in which every eligible block satisfies the hypotheses of Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4, there are constants \(C,C_0<\infty\), common to the eligible blocks for all sufficiently large \(n\), such that
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 \le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
No assertion that the last sum vanishes, and no uniform \(O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) assertion over \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), is made.
body.justification: This theorem supplies the exact bridge from blockwise debiasing to the adoption-aligned event score and records precisely what a simultaneous source-level remainder event would deliver.
body.gap: Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 is one-block and i.i.d. homoskedastic; direct aggregation over growing eligible blocks yields a finite union bound, not a class-uniform stochastic remainder rate.
body.consumer: The eventwise identity and explicit failure sum are inputs to the finite-error whole-curve bound and to diagnostics for a right-to-carry event plot.
body.proof_tex:
For a fixed eligible pair \((g,k)\), the definition of \(r_{gk}\) is an
exact equality.  The eligible estimator and target satisfy, respectively,
\[
 \widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\widehat\tau_{gk},
 \qquad
 \tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}\tau_{gk}.
\]
The second equality follows from \(N_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}n_g\) and the
definition of \(\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\).  Subtracting these equalities and
substituting the exact block decompositions gives
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}
   \sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
All sums are finite.  Hence their order may be interchanged.  The definition
of the exact aggregated coefficient gives
\[
 \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}b_{gk,q}=c_{kq},
\]
and therefore
\[
 \widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q
  +\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Assumption \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\) gives \(s_k>0\).
Since \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), division by \(s_k\) yields
\[
 s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\sum_q a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q}
  +s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Comparison with the definition of \(\rho_{n,k}\) proves both the coordinate
identity and the displayed formula for \(\rho_{n,k}\); stacking the finite
collection of coordinates proves the vector identity.

On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), positivity of \(n_g/N_k\), the triangle inequality,
and the definition of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty
 &\le \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}|r_{gk}|\\
 &\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
       \sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\\
 &=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
 \end{aligned}
\]

It remains to justify the finite probability statement in the stated source
submodel.  Apply \(\texttt{lem:choi-yuan-one-block-remainder}\) separately to
each eligible block.  In the notation of that cited proposition, the missing
group size is \(\vartheta_o=n_g\), the block dimensions are \(N_o=N_{gk}\)
and \(T_o=T_g\), and the proposition's three displayed remainder terms are
exactly those collected in \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  For a treated row
\(i\in I_g\), Proposition A.4 writes the imputation error as its donor-column
linear term, its treated-row pre-period linear term, and an entry remainder
\(\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}\).  Since
\[
 Y_{i,g+k}-m^0_{i,g+k}-\tau_{i,g+k}=e_{i,g+k},
\]
subtracting the imputation expansion and averaging over \(i\in I_g\) gives
the displayed block expansion with
\[
 r_{gk}=-\frac1{n_g}\sum_{i\in I_g}\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}.
\]
Thus \(\max_{i\in I_g}|\mathcal R^M_{gk,i}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\)
implies \(|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  The uniform block ratios in
the source submodel and the common constants in the frozen class make the
constant in the cited one-block bound common to eligible blocks once \(n\) is
sufficiently large.  Consequently,
\[
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}
 \le C_0\min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
Boole's inequality over the finite set of eligible pairs now gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 &\le\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 P_n\{|r_{gk}|>C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}\\
 &\le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is only a finite union bound.  None of the frozen assumptions forces its
right-hand side to tend to zero, which is why the theorem makes no stronger
stochastic-order claim.
